findings.explanation: The PR diff replaces a parameterized query (cur.execute("SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname=%s;", (db_name,))) with a string-formatted one (cur.execute("SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname='{}';".format(db_name))). The db_name value is user-controlled: in postgraas_server/management_resources.py (lines 130-144) the 'db_name' argument is parsed directly from the HTTP request body (parser.add_argument('db_name', required=True, type=str)) with no validation or whitelist, then placed into db_credentials and passed to current_app.postgraas_backend.create(db_entry, db_credentials). That flows to PGClusterBackend.create (backends/postgres_cluster/__init__.py:9-14) -> pgcd.create_postgres_db -> check_db_or_user_exists(connection_dict['db_name'], ...), where the value is interpolated into the SQL string via .format(). An attacker can supply a db_name like "x'; DROP DATABASE y; --" to break out of the quoted literal and inject arbitrary SQL. The base branch (line 23) was safe (parameterized), so this is a genuine regression introduced by the PR.
